notes: Route: the prior Home-Decor pass concluded only WebFetch worked, because this is a fully client-side-rendered NetSuite SuiteCommerce Advanced (SCA) storefront. This pass found the SCA Items service instead, and it is served unauthenticated to a plain desktop UA: https://www.scullyandscully.com/api/items?limit=1&custitem_is_subitem=false&commercecategoryurl=<category path> returns {"total": N}. robots.txt explicitly ALLOWS ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / Claude-SearchBot (no Claude-specific disallow); its only Disallow rules cover /search, /checkout, /my_account and sort/filter query URLs, none of which were used. CRITICAL calibration: the raw API total is inflated because it counts matrix sub-items. Adding custitem_is_subitem=false reproduces the site's own rendered '#### N Products' listing header exactly. Validated against the rendered header via WebFetch on 6 pages: /furniture 620 vs 620, seating/armchairs 70 vs 70 (raw API said 74 - this is why the filter is required), tables/side-tables 71 vs 71, cabinets-bookcases-chests/cabinets-cupboards 64 vs 64, seating/sofas-loveseats 18 vs 18, miscellaneous/etageres 3 vs 3. Every qty below is the filtered API total, i.e. the rendered header number. Tree source: the complete mega-menu is present server-side in the homepage HTML (485 anchors parsed with BeautifulSoup); cross-checked against the rendered /furniture department page via WebFetch, whose 8 second-level nodes and their children match exactly, so the tree is complete. Furniture exists only under the /furniture department. The whole nav (jewelry, home-decor, tabletop, collectibles, herend, gift-ideas, inspiration, new-arrivals) was reviewed and holds no furniture-typed nodes - home-decor carries lamps, mirrors, clocks, picture frames, trays, vases, fire screens, umbrella stands, wastebaskets and desk accessories, all decor/accessory rather than furniture. All 8 second-level nodes (Seating, Cabinets/Bookcases/Chests, Tables, Folding Furniture, Office, Beds, Contemporary, Miscellaneous) have children, so all are emitted as grouping rows and only the leaves carry qty and link. EXCLUDED: every 'Shop All ...' rollup under each parent, per the NEVER-EXTRACT list. Those rollups are also smaller than the sum of their siblings (Shop All Tables 206 vs children summing 268), which shows the site cross-lists items across sibling leaves; no sums or aggregates were used anywhere. EXCLUDED Beds > 'Bedding & Linens' (6) as textiles. EXCLUDED Miscellaneous > 'Eco-Friendly Furniture' (39, /furniture/miscellaneous/eco-friendly-frie-furniture): it is an attribute cross-cut, and all 39 tiles were listed via the API - they are dominated by wastebaskets, umbrella stands, hampers, trays, wall shelves and a storage box, so the products clearly contradict the Furniture filing. DE-DUPLICATED 'Desk Chairs': it is cross-listed in the nav under both Seating (/furniture/seating/desk-chairs) and Office (/furniture/office/desk-chairs), and both return the same total of 19, so it is emitted once under Seating; Office therefore keeps Desks, Writing Tables and Filing Cabinets. Ambiguous nodes were resolved by listing their real product tiles through the API (fields=displayname) rather than by guessing - see the flags on Jewelry & Silver Chests, Luggage Racks and Other Furniture. Sanity checks: totals differ per category (no constant site-wide number); no suspiciously round display caps; the department total 620 is far below the sum of its leaves, so it is a genuine de-duplicated department figure and not an aggregate; the parent nodes Seating, Cabinets/Bookcases/Chests, Folding Furniture, Office, Contemporary and Miscellaneous each return total=0 directly, which is what identifies them as pure grouping nodes. Minor drift versus the prior Home-Decor pass was seen on unrelated decor categories (rectangular-mirrors 80 -> 81, mantel-desk-clocks 81 -> 85), consistent with ordinary catalogue churn since that session; all furniture numbers here are fresh reads taken in this session.
